context: Theorem II.4. Let D = {DN }N ≥1 be a distribution ensemble, where each DN is supported over {0, 1}N . The following results hold: (i) Let C be a nice class of Boolean circuits, and suppose D admits implicit DLOGTIME-uniform C-samplers of size polylog(N ). (ii) Suppose D admits a polynomial-time sampler of randomness complexity (log N )O(1) . Then, for every function δ(N ) = 1/(log N )k , where k ∈ N, there is a polynomial-time pseudodeterministic algorithm for the (D, δ)-Heavy-Avoid problem that succeeds on infinitely many inputs.8 (iii) Suppose D admits a polynomial-time sampler. Then, for every function δ(N ) = 1/N k , where k ∈ N, and for every constant ε > 0, there is a pseudodeterministic algorithm for the (D, δ)-Heavy-Avoid problem that runs in time ε 2N and succeeds on infinitely many inputs. Moreover, in all items the corresponding algorithm behaves pseudodeterministically on every input.
